key_insight: The paper shows that high-energy physics jet models follow robust scaling laws, enabling principled choices of model size, data size, and training hyperparameters under compute or data limits.
engineering_relevance: These results provide a practical recipe for optimizing HEP foundation models, helping engineers allocate compute and dataset scale more efficiently while comparing architecture choices fairly.
method: Validate full scaling trajectories on toy problems first.
Apply the procedure to multi-task transformers on the ~11B-jet ATLAS JetSet2 dataset.
Analyze both compute-constrained and data-constrained regimes, including early-stopping optima.
evidence_signal: The study reports near-√C joint scaling of model and dataset size at compute optimum, and tests how auxiliary objectives and lower-level inputs affect jet-classification loss on the large JetSet2 dataset.
watch_item: Scaling conclusions may not transfer below the dataset-size threshold where the power-law regime is not yet informative, so small or low-quality datasets can give misleading extrapolations.
paper_title: How to scale your HEP ML models: A recipe for robust architecture comparisons at scale
